text:
maria: Heads-up — received a customer report: their request sometimes hits the wrong backend when both X-Env and X-Stage headers are present. Repro on staging
kevin: Ugh. Any chance it's the new header-priority changes from last week?
liz: I saw a flaky test in the routing suite earlier that looked similar — headers with numeric weight + multiple matchers.
maria: Pasting the route they sent (redacted):
```yaml
- name: billing-route
  match:
    headers:
      - name: X-Env
        value: production
        weight: 10
      - name: X-Stage
        value: canary
        weight: 10
  priority: 100
  backend: billing-v2
- name: billing-fallback
  match:
    headers:
      - name: X-Env
        value: production
  priority: 50
  backend: billing-v1
```
kevin: Hmm the equal weights could be triggering a non-deterministic tiebreaker. Our resolver used to stable-sort by header name, but I changed it to sort by insertion order to respect author intent. Maybe insertion order isn't stable across caller paths.
sam: Can we reproduce locally? Maria, do you have a minimal curl that shows the wrong backend?
maria: Yep — here's a trimmed trace (staging):
```
POST /api/payments 200 OK -> backend: billing-v1
headers: X-Env: production, X-Stage: canary
```
kevin: That log proves the fallback route matched even though the first route should have matched both headers. Two suspects: 1) header matcher normalization (case or whitespace), 2) priority resolver tie behavior.
liz: I ran the unit test with a seed and got differing outcomes across runs (seed 42 vs seed 43). So non-determinism for sure.
config-bot: LINT >> header_matchers: unstable-ordering detected in routes/billing-route.yaml (severity=warning)
sam: We should add a deterministic canonicalization step: sort by (name, value, weight) and then apply insertion order only when fully equal. Low-risk patch.
kevin: Agreed. Also add a lint rule to flag equal-weight multiple headers that could cause ambiguous intent. Customer-facing UX: console should show a preview explaining how tie-breaks are resolved.
maria: For the immediate customer fix, can we push a patch to make the resolver deterministic and roll it to staging today?
liz: I can open a tiny PR: change resolver sort key to tuple (name.lower(), value, weight, original_index). Tests + fuzz should run.
kevin: Also add a tiny e2e that spins up two routes like in the repro and asserts stable backend selection over 100 runs.
config-bot: CI >> routing-unit-tests passed (changed files: routing/resolver.py, tests/test_header_tiebreak.py)
maria: Thanks. After PR lands, I'll re-run the customer's test and report back. :thumbsup:
kevin: Filing a short postmortem note once we confirm. We might also update console docstring for header priority to avoid future confusion.
liz: One more: add a lint autofix option that reorders headers into canonical order and shows a diff in the console preflight. Could make UX smoother.
sam: SGTM. I'll coordinate rollout schedule with infra so canary sees it first.
maria: Perfect. Closing loop after staging verify.
